Irene / Marissa — quick heads up and a specific ask before our next customer touchpoint. BrightByte Financial (contact: Sarah Liu) is moving from POC to contract stage and has one blocking runtime ask: per-customer model affinity + deterministic fallback policy. In short they want to pin a primary model per-tenant and a configurable fallback chain (e.g., cheaper quantized variant, alternate region, or cached-response mode) that we can turn on for specific accounts during peak or regulatory review windows.

Why this matters: BrightByte is enterprise-sized, will commit to a 3-year reserved plan if we give them both (1) predictable latency for their Tier-1 flows and (2) a watertight fallback strategy that preserves privacy/compliance during audit holds. This is the kind of anchor account that unlocks our Dedicated bookings.

What I need from Product/Eng (concrete):
- A one-page tradeoff matrix comparing 3 approaches (routing-only config, affinity+cache shim, model-variant support) across columns: latency impact (p50/p95), estimated per-token cost delta, security/regulatory risk, and rough eng LOE (T-shirt: S/M/L).
- A two-slide summary we can show execs and BrightByte on the Nov 19 call (they asked for internal confirmation by then).
- A proposal for the earliest feasible roadmap slot (we're targeting an initial customer-facing rollout in Q1).

Attachments: BB-HB4829-deal-onepager.pdf, BB-costing-estimates.xlsx. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4829.

Timing: BrightByte expects a decision before our call on Nov 19. If we can get the tradeoff matrix + LOE by COB Nov 24 I can lock the commitment.

Notes: I recognize this touches product/infra and may require a short design spike. I'm asking for prioritization guidance and a small scope we can propose to the customer to accelerate signing.

Ben

Thanks — answers inline below (quoting your questions):

> 1) Scope: per-tenant or per-route?
Per-tenant. BrightByte's compliance model is tenant-scoped; they want a single control plane knob per tenant that pins the primary model and configures fallback order. Per-route granularity would be ideal later, but per-tenant is the immediate ask.

> 2) Success metrics: p95 target, cost ceiling?
They asked for p95 <= 300ms for the three Tier-1 flows, and said they will accept up to ~20% per-token cost increase for stronger guarantees, provided we offer toggles they can flip. They also care about deterministic behavior during audit windows (no cross-tenant caching that might leak).

> 3) Compliance needs: data residency or policy-driven fallback?
Policy-driven fallback is fine initially, but with a clear requirement that the fallback path also respects residency bounds (i.e., fallbacks must stay in region EMEA/US as applicable).

I've uploaded a small costing sheet with their expected QPS and token mix: BB-costing-estimates.xlsx. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4829.

Ask to Product/Eng: would a scoped "customer-affinity + fallback chain" feature be workable as a Q1 pilot if we limit rollout to 1 customer and expose config via Console + API? If yes, what is Jordan's LOE estimate for each option?

Ben

Appreciate the clear ask — marking this high priority for Sales-driven pilots. Jordan — can you add LOE estimates to the attached tradeoff template and pick one recommended path (we'll present tradeoffs + recommended option to BrightByte). My suggested options for recommendation: 

A) Fast path (shim): routing config + console toggle to enforce primary+fallback. Minimal infra changes, SLO risk depends on fallback latency.
B) Medium path (affinity + cache): add per-tenant affinity routing with small cache layer for repeated prompts; better latency stability but medium LOE.
C) Full path (model variants + analytics): support pinned model variants per tenant plus monitoring/rollback hooks; highest LOE but best long-term product fit.

Proposed near-term plan: Jordan and Irene produce the filled matrix + LOE by COB Nov 24. If LOE is S/M/L as expected, we can offer a Q1 pilot slot (week of Jan 8) for a constrained rollout (BrightByte only) and use that to refine cost controls before broader availability.
